slot.brief: Find intervals where a simple polynomial or x³ − 3x-type function is increasing/decreasing using the sign of f′(x).

stem: For $f(x)=x^3+3x^2$, the maximal interval on which $f$ is decreasing is

verdicts.working: f'(x)=3x(x+2), which is nonpositive on [-2,0] and positive outside. Thus the maximal decreasing interval is [-2,0].

working:
$f'(x)=3x(x+2)$.\n$f'(x)<0$ for $-2<x<0$; $f'(-2)=f'(0)=0$.\nThus $f$ is decreasing on the maximal interval $[-2,0]$.

Independent check: f'(x)=3x(x+2), which is nonpositive on [-2,0] and positive outside. Thus the maximal decreasing interval is [-2,0].
solution:
$$f'(x)=3x(x+2).$$
Since $f'(x)\le 0$ for $-2\le x\le 0$ and is positive outside this interval, $f$ is decreasing on the maximal interval $[-2,0]$.
